![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14067291/assets/6accbfcccdf910acca3aab9f1a12d0ab35c4da683fe78d6ca2d7ada88f28767c.png)

Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\,dA,$
where $D$ is the finite region above the $x$-axis enclosed by the curve $y=1-{x}^{2}$ and the line $x=0.$
worked_solution:
Notice that $D$ is a type I region.

- We already know the intersection of the curve with the line $y=0.$
So, the $x$-limits are 
$0\le x\le 1.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14067291/assets/db0dd47348fb2f9a97c9e0514f74adae05830de7e03f1aea2886eaa95701200e.png)

As a result, the integral is defined over the following type I region: 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1-{x}^{2}}
$$

So, we can express the integral, as follows:

$$
{∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\,dA={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}{x}^{2}\,dy\,dx
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}{x}^{2}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}[y]_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{2}-0)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\,dx & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5}-0 \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\end{aligned}
$$
